evals.prompt: Build the architecture model for the successful Search Opportunities operation from the supplied synthetic repositories. Use Opportunity as the domain. Trace every evidenced web/mobile caller through the Search API and all downstream work to the returned response. Save the complete .architecture-model directory as the output.
evals.expected_output: A valid sharded schema-version-2 graph with a compact generated index, reciprocal domain/component/operation hierarchy, one successful operation path, and deterministic numbered/ASCII projections.
expectations: No model.json exists and index.json contains references, hashes, and hierarchy rather than copied architecture records.
The domain references stable component and operation shards, and each component-operation link is reciprocal.
Both web and mobile callers are corroborated by outbound route/version evidence and represented as caller relationships.

The canonical path numbers and orders authentication/controller handling, handler dispatch, LaunchDarkly, local configuration, Elasticsearch, SQL, Eligibility, Details, telemetry, response mapping, and final caller return without inventing a message bus.
Local options access is a local config-read step rather than an external configuration runtime.
Eligibility and Details continuations are traced into supplied repositories rather than stopping at the first outbound edge.
The path participant set exactly matches touched nodes/components and excludes unrelated elements.
The generated numbered Markdown and ASCII projections pass deterministic validation against the canonical path.

evals.prompt: Starting only with the search-api directory in the opportunity-system fixture, discover and record repositories needed for upstream caller and downstream continuation analysis. Do not silently scan a repository before adding it to the persisted source queue.
evals.expected_output: The Search API scan records candidate repositories with reasons/evidence/status, accepted candidates receive source shards and progress entries, and unavailable or rejected candidates remain visible.
expectations: Repository discovery is persisted in scan.discoveredRepositories instead of conversation-only notes.
Each candidate has a stable source ID, location or repository identity, reason, evidence, and explicit status.
Accepted repositories are added to subject requestedSources, domain sourceIds, progress sources, and source shards before scanning.
The agent does not claim web/mobile callers without their outbound evidence and records missing caller discovery as a gap when those repositories are unavailable.

evals.prompt: Copy the supplied complete order-submission example twice. On the second copy, reorder set-like JSON arrays and object keys without changing facts. Run format, render, index, validate, and compare the indexes.
evals.expected_output: Both copies converge to the same canonical semantic model and byte-identical projections, with no semantic or projection changes.
expectations: Both final modelSemanticHash values are equal.
The diff has no added, removed, semanticChanges, evidenceOnlyChanges, or projectionChanges entries.
Numbered Markdown and ASCII outputs are byte-identical after rendering.
Both models pass final validation.

evals.prompt: Using copies of the complete order-submission example, first change only evidence line ranges and source revision, then separately change the handler responsibility and insert a real dependency step. Rebuild and compare each snapshot.
evals.expected_output: The first comparison is provenance/evidence-only; the second identifies semantic changes limited to affected component/path/relationship artifacts and regenerated projections.
expectations: Line/revision-only edits do not change modelSemanticHash and are reported as evidenceOnlyChanges or source-only provenance changes.
A changed component responsibility is reported as a component semantic change.
An inserted dependency changes the relevant relationship/path and generated projections rather than unrelated shards.
The change report does not describe every artifact as modified.

evals.prompt: Mutate the complete example's ASCII projection by reversing one arrow and renaming one operation without changing the canonical path. Attempt final validation, then regenerate projections and validate again.
evals.expected_output: Validation fails closed on projection drift; deterministic render repairs both views from the canonical path and final validation succeeds.
expectations: Validation fails before regeneration and identifies deterministic projection drift.
The canonical path is not changed merely to agree with the tampered projection.
Render restores exact sequence numbers, labels, endpoints, direction, input/output, and outcome.
A second render is byte-identical and final validation succeeds.

evals.prompt: Model a POST handler that returns HTTP 202 after publishing OpportunityChanged v3, plus a supplied v3 indexing worker and an incompatible legacy v2 worker. Produce reviewable paths without flattening incompatible or asynchronous behavior.
evals.expected_output: Separate linked accepted-response and background-completion paths, with publish/channel/delivery/consume/store/telemetry order, v3 continuation, and a preserved v2 conflict.
expectations: The HTTP accepted path has its own terminal caller return.
The asynchronous completion path links through causedByPathIds or continuesFromPathIds and correlation metadata.
Publish, channel, subscription delivery, consume, data read, index write, telemetry, and terminal effect are separate ordered steps.
The v2 worker is represented as an incompatibility conflict, not merged into the successful v3 path.
Both paths have independently generated numbered and ASCII projections.
